messages:
Jordan W: Quick sync — I drafted a short proposal to simplify the runtime contract between hosted / dedicated / private. Wanted early feedback before I write an RFC.

Jordan W: Problem: we keep re-implementing slightly different probes, lease semantics, and token passthrough for each hosting mode which makes edge cases (eviction, failover, audit) explode.

Meera K: 👍 can you paste the minimal contract you have in mind?

Jordan W: Sure — idea is a tiny delegation/proxy surface that focuses on: capability token exchange, a bounded lease, and a single-call fallback path. Example pseudo-interface:
```
interface DelegateAgent {
  Serve(req: Request, token: CapabilityToken): Response
  Heartbeat(leaseID: string): OK|Err
  Drain(leaseID: string): Ack
}
```

Jordan W: Rationale: keep runtime code paths identical across modes. Hosted returns token A, dedicated returns token A+affinity, private returns token A with tenant-scoped keys. Upstream code only calls Serve + Heartbeat.

Liam T: This seems promising. Two quick questions: (1) how are secrets handled for private (on-prem) agents? (2) what about observability correlation if the proxy masquerades as the runtime?

Jordan W: For secrets: token contains a short-lived capability referencing a KMS-wrapped credential stored in the control plane. On private, the control plane only issues references; customer KMS unwraps in their network. So the agent only ever holds ephemeral tokens.

Samir P: Observability: agree with minimal surface, but we need a stable trace/span convention so telemetry shows both delegator and delegate. Proposal: delegator injects header x-rw-delegation-id and the agent attaches both its span and that header to exported traces.

Meera K: Eviction semantics still worry me. Hosted can abort quickly; dedicated needs graceful drain; private might be opaque. Do we force a common lease behavior or allow mode-specific tuning?

Jordan W: My thought: common lease contract with three levels: soft, graceful, hard. Lease message includes TTL + preferredDrainSeconds + evictionPolicy enum (soft/graceful/hard). Agents must implement behavior consistent with the enum but may surface telemetry for mode-specific delays.

Liam T: Implementation nit: prefer lease IDs be cryptographically unguessable and tied to capability token to prevent cross-tenant reuse. Also Lease Heartbeat should be idempotent.

Samir P: Can we make Drain synchronous (wait for in-flight tokenized KV cache to flush) but with a deadline so callers can fallback to ServeFallback?

Jordan W: Yes — Drain(leaseID, deadline) -> Ack|Timeout. Caller gets Timeout and can call ServeFallback for stateless cheap variant.

Meera K: Suggest we add a tiny health check endpoint that returns (mode, leaseState, tokenSchemaVersion) so deployment tooling can act without guessing.

Jordan W: Good call. I'll add that: /_agent_meta -> {mode, leaseID?, tokensSchema, lastHeartbeat} as read-only.

ops-bot: Note: created ticket INF-3421 from this thread (delegation proxy minimal contract).

Liam T: One more tradeoff — cost/latency: adding an extra delegation hop increases p50 by ~1-3ms in prod estimates. We should test in a canary.

Jordan W: Agreed. Plan: I'll turn this into an RFC draft with the interface + examples and a canary plan (hosted first, dedicated next). Meera/Liam/Samir can we pair on the telemetry/eviction sections?

Meera K: I can take telemetry + audit.

Liam T: I'll do latency experiments and the canary plan.

Samir P: I'll write the private-KMS/secretflow section.

Jordan W: Thanks — will drop RFC link here when ready. :party-parrot:

ops-bot: INF-3421 updated: assignees Meera K, Liam T, Samir P. Due: 2025-11-15.
